summary: Captopril is the prototype sulfhydryl-containing ACE inhibitor used for hypertension, heart failure, left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction, and diabetic nephropathy. It suppresses the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, lowering blood pressure and afterload. It carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity and must be taken one hour before meals because food reduces its absorption. Key risks are angioedema, hyperkalemia, cough, and neutropenia.
indications: Congestive heart failure (usually with diuretics and digitalis)
Left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction (to improve survival)

dosage.d: Initial 25 mg twice or three times daily; may increase to 50 mg 2-3 times daily after 1-2 weeks
dosage.n: Take 1 hour before meals; usual max 50 mg three times daily

dosage.d: Initial 25 mg three times daily (6.25-12.5 mg if on diuretic/low BP); target 50 mg three times daily
Start 6.25 mg single dose, then 12.5 mg three times daily; increase over several days to 25 mg three times daily, then target 50 mg three times daily
dosage.n: Begin as early as 3 days post-MI
For type 1 diabetic nephropathy with proteinuria

admin: Take one hour before meals (food reduces absorption by 30-40%)
First dose may cause excessive hypotension - especially if volume/salt depleted or on a diuretic
Avoid potassium supplements and potassium-sparing diuretics unless directed
moa: Captopril competitively inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE, peptidyl-dipeptidase), preventing conversion of angiotensin I to the potent vasoconstrictor angiotensin II. This reduces vasoconstriction and aldosterone secretion (lowering sodium/water retention) and decreases degradation of bradykinin. The net effect is reduced peripheral resistance and blood pressure, and reduced cardiac afterload, with suppression of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to captopril or any ACE inhibitor (including prior ACE-inhibitor angioedema)
Concomitant aliskiren in patients with diabetes
Use within 36 hours of sacubitril/valsartan (neprilysin inhibitor)
Pregnancy (fetal toxicity - discontinue when pregnancy detected)
relative: Collagen vascular disease with renal impairment (neutropenia risk)

preg: Boxed warning: drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause fetal injury and death (oligohydramnios, renal failure, skull hypoplasia, hypotension). Discontinue captopril as soon as pregnancy is detected.
lact: Captopril is excreted in breast milk in small concentrations; generally considered compatible with breastfeeding when use is necessary, with monitoring of the infant.
renal: Captopril is retained in renal impairment. Reduce initial dose and extend dosing interval; titrate slowly. Monitor serum creatinine and potassium closely, particularly in renal artery stenosis or volume depletion.
hepatic: Rare cholestatic jaundice progressing to fulminant hepatic necrosis has occurred; discontinue if marked elevation of hepatic enzymes or jaundice develops. Use with caution in hepatic impairment.

major: Aliskiren (contraindicated in diabetes; dual RAAS blockade risks hyperkalemia, hypotension, renal failure)
Sacubitril/valsartan (neprilysin inhibitor - angioedema risk; separate by 36 hours)
moderate: NSAIDs (reduced antihypertensive effect, renal deterioration, hyperkalemia)
mTOR inhibitors (sirolimus, everolimus) - increased angioedema risk
interactions.food: Food reduces absorption by 30-40%; take one hour before meals. Limit high-potassium foods and salt substitutes.
interactions.alcohol: May potentiate the blood-pressure-lowering effect; limit intake
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine acetone test; can elevate serum potassium, creatinine, and BUN

monitoring: Blood pressure (especially after first dose and dose changes)
White blood cell and differential count (baseline and periodically, especially in renal/collagen vascular disease)
counsel: Take one hour before meals at the same times each day
Stop the drug and seek urgent care for swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or difficulty breathing
Report persistent dry cough, sore throat with fever, fainting, or reduced urination
Do not use potassium supplements or salt substitutes unless told to
Tell your doctor immediately if you become or plan to become pregnant
Rise slowly to avoid dizziness, especially when starting therapy
pk: Antihypertensive effect within 15-60 minutes of an oral dose
Peak blood levels at about 1 hour; peak BP effect 60-90 minutes
Less than 2-3 hours (prolonged in renal impairment)
Dose-related, generally 6-12 hours; requires multiple daily dosing
Store at controlled room temperature 20-25 C; protect from moisture
pearls: Prototype ACE inhibitor with a sulfhydryl group, linked historically to taste disturbance and rash
Short half-life requires 2-3 times daily dosing, unlike longer-acting ACE inhibitors
Must be taken one hour before meals because food cuts absorption by 30-40%
Dry cough is a class effect from reduced bradykinin breakdown; switch to an ARB if intolerable
Black patients and those with low-renin hypertension may respond less to monotherapy
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember (one hour before a meal if possible). If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Overdose causes marked hypotension. Management is supportive: place patient supine, give intravenous normal saline for volume expansion to restore blood pressure; consider angiotensin II or catecholamines if needed. Captopril is removed by hemodialysis. Monitor potassium and renal function.
